evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形; Mandarin readings; senses under jiào and xiào
evidence.text: The entry repeats the Shuowen analysis 木囚也、从木交聲 and gives the Mandarin readings jiào and xiào. It separately cites restraint (including the received Yijing line 何校滅耳), barrier, horse and military organizations, textual correction, and a school sense in Mengzi. These cited uses do not establish a securely dated sequence of semantic change.
evidence.title: [A01910] 校 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.field: 校 entry; definition and component analysis
evidence.text: The entry reads 校（ ）：木囚也。從木交聲. Xu Shen’s Han-period dictionary account glosses 校 as a wooden restraint and assigns 木 a semantic role and 交 a phonetic role. This is a historical lexicographic claim, not independent proof of the graph’s earliest form or use.
evidence.title: 說文解字/06

evidence.field: 校; forms, pronunciation, historical citations and semantic account
evidence.text: The page displays a small-seal form and manuscript-form images, but no oracle-bone or bronze example for 校 in its displayed form inventory. It reports received-text citations for a restraint, barrier, military organization, checking/collation, and school. Its semantic discussion proposes barrier-related extension for some uses, but the page’s citation list does not independently date those transitions. The transmitted Mengzi passage has 夏曰校 and explains 校者教也; it attests a school-related use in that text, not a demonstrated route from ‘restraint’ or ‘barrier’.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 校

evidence.field: 交; current Mandarin, Shuowen account, and historical form discussion
evidence.text: The page gives current Mandarin jiāo and repeats the Shuowen description 交脛也。从大，象交形. Its own account describes early forms as a variant of 大 depicting a person with crossed legs; it discusses disputed identifications of an alleged oracle-bone form and gives bronze, bamboo-slip, and transmitted-text uses. This describes the history of 交 as a character; it does not establish an original name or pronunciation for a physical tool supposedly meant by 校.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 交

gaps: No independently dated oracle-bone, bronze, or other early inscription for 校 was verified. The CUHK page displays small-seal and manuscript image slots but does not provide a dated early sequence in the inspected text.

The relation between the restraint sense and the school sense is unresolved. The transmitted Mengzi passage attests a school-related use, but a path through barrier or enclosure is not established by the inspected evidence.

Classical citations separately attest restraint, barrier, military organization, checking/collation, and school uses. Their earliest attestations and a secure chronological chain remain unresolved; dictionary citation order is not treated as chronology.

Shuowen and the Taiwan Ministry dictionary assert 交 as the phonetic component. The supplied Baxter–Sagart table gives 交 *[k]ˤraw but no 校 row, so comparable same-system reconstructions were not recovered. Dossier reconstructions are not assigned a verified system here.

Exact local readings are recorded as provided rows: 交 jiāo and 校 xiào from sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt; exact local 交 Baxter–Sagart row is *[k]ˤraw from sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv. These are not independent proof of ancient sound correspondence. Unicode’s exact character pages were inaccessible.

The exact Commons 交 seal candidates were not accessible in this session; their identity, provenance, dating, and reuse terms remain unverified. Do not treat the candidate filenames or the 校 Shuowen-style redraw as archaeological glyph evidence.

The Shuowen wooden-restraint gloss does not independently recover the physical object’s original name or pronunciation, and no whole-graph phonetic loan is established. The phonetic-component claim is kept separate from any hypothetical loan claim.
